audience.notes: Australian couples in their 30s, AUD 150K+, paying venues and suppliers in euros or other currencies from home. Couple fear 4: currencies and contracts. Parent reads for who handles the money, currency surprises and safety of large transfers. Not a 'cheapest way to send money' piece.

payload.search_intent: Informational how-to: how to pay overseas vendors, in what currency, by what method, on what schedule, and how to avoid losing money. SERPs are forum-led (AU and UK), so the question is live but unowned.
payload.angle: The Australian couple's guide to paying overseas vendors without surprises: how deposits and balances run abroad, who carries the exchange-rate risk between deposit and balance, what to compare between payment methods in general terms, what to do when a vendor asks for cash, and how to stop invoice scams, with official sources at each claim and the payment schedule a Wedded Advisor coordinates across every supplier.
serp_gaps_to_win: AU top 3 are Facebook and Reddit threads, mostly on tipping; no Australian brand or official-source page answers how to pay an overseas vendor.
London top 3 are forums asking how to pay Italian vendors and whether to pay balances in cash; nobody answers with a plan.
No ranking page covers invoice and payment-redirection scams, currency risk between deposit and balance, or tying payments to cancellation terms and insurance.
Commercial results are FX providers with savings claims; a general-information page with Moneysmart, Scamwatch and ACCC sources is the trustworthy alternative.
Related searches show 'reddit' and 'cost' modifiers: readers want real-world answers and what paying abroad adds to the cost.

outline.h2: What changes when you pay a wedding vendor overseas
outline.answers: Why paying abroad differs from home: another currency, another country's consumer law, transfer fees and margins, time zones, and less recourse if something goes wrong.
must_include: General-information line near the top: check with your bank or a licensed adviser (Nic or legal confirms wording)
Moneysmart on international transfers, rates and fees at the claim
Link /destination-weddings/hidden-costs-destination-wedding

outline.h2: How deposits, instalments and final balances usually run abroad
outline.answers: Typical structure (deposit to hold the date, staged payments, balance before the day), why each contract sets its own dates, and refundable bonds as a separate line.
must_include: Our live wording only: deposits 'ran from 10% to 50% of the total' on vendor terms read, balances '180 days to 72 hours' before (from /expert-advice/wedding-expenses-spreadsheet, quote as worded and link it)
ACCC on deposits and refunds at the claim (reused)
Link /planning/wedding-vendor-list-template and /expert-advice/wedding-expenses-spreadsheet
No invented percentages; do not repeat competitor '25 to 50 percent' or '30 to 60 days'

outline.h2: Which currency to pay in, and who carries the exchange-rate risk
outline.answers: Quote in the vendor's currency vs an AUD quote, how the AUD cost of a euro balance moves between deposit and balance, why to budget a currency buffer, and asking what rate an AUD quote uses.
must_include: Worked example in words only, no live rates or forecasts; any example figures labelled as illustrative
Link /destination-weddings/destination-wedding-budget ONLY when LIVE (DRAFT, RETRO-LINK)
Link /travel-guides/travel-advisor-benefits (AUD quotes, as worded there)

outline.h2: Bank transfer, card or transfer service: what to compare
outline.answers: In general terms: the rate offered vs the mid-market rate, fees on both ends, speed, whether the vendor's bank charges to receive, and card protections as the issuer's terms state them.
must_include: No named banks, transfer services or card products; no rankings, rates, fees or 'cheapest' claims (FIN-ADVICE-CHECK)
Moneysmart at the claim
AUSTRAC: money transfer services in Australia must be registered (only as an official page states it)
Chargeback only as a general 'check your card issuer's terms'

outline.h2: When a vendor asks for the balance in cash
outline.answers: Why some vendors abroad ask for cash, asking for a written receipt, how to carry or withdraw it, and tips in local currency.
must_include: Smartraveller on money overseas
AUD 10,000 or more cash declaration only if an AUSTRAC or ABF page states it; otherwise [[NEEDS]]
Receipts kept for insurance claims (link /destination-weddings/wedding-insurance)

outline.h2: How to protect every payment from invoice scams
outline.answers: Payment-redirection and fake-invoice scams, verifying bank details by phone on a known number before the first transfer and after any change, and what to do if money goes to the wrong account.
must_include: Scamwatch on payment redirection at the claim
Our live wording: 'Verify unexpected changes to supplier bank details directly before transferring funds' (vendor list template)
Link /how-to-choose-wedding-vendors-abroad

outline.h2: Matching each payment to its contract, cancellation terms and insurance
outline.answers: Who signs and pays each contract (including parents paying for events), cancellation cutoffs set against payment dates, keeping proof of payment, and buying wedding insurance once the first deposit is paid.
must_include: Paying-parent fear: who handles the money; if a parent pays, whose name is on the contract
Link /destination-weddings/wedding-insurance (do not repeat its insurer names or limits)

outline.h2: What your Wedded Advisor handles on payments
outline.answers: The invisible work: one payment schedule across every supplier, each in its own currency, due dates and reminders, inclusions confirmed in writing, bank details checked, and currency and international payments coordinated.
must_include: Concierge in brand-profile wording only ('currency and international payments coordinated'); no Concierge prices
Studio as worded on /wonderland-studio: 'Set a budget, log deposits and see what is left in every category'; no multi-currency claim
Link /wonderland-concierge
